Classic prisoner's dilemma!

This is a classic problem in game theory, and there's no one "right" answer. However, I'll provide some insights.

From a rational perspective, you would want to do what's best for yourself, regardless of what others do. Since the outcome depends on the majority vote, your goal should be to make sure that you are part of the majority.

If you think most people will press the blue button (the "cooperative" option), then it's rational to also press the blue button. This way, you'll be part of the majority and ensure your own survival.

On the other hand, if you think most people will press the red button (the "defection" option), then it might be better for you to also press the red button. This way, you'll at least have a chance to survive, even if everyone else dies.

However, this is where things get tricky. If you're the only one who presses the blue button when most people are pressing the red button, you'll be a martyr and won't survive. And if you're the only one who presses the red button when most people are pressing the blue button, you'll be a defector and won't survive either.

So, what to do?

In this situation, it's not possible to know for certain what others will do, so there is an element of uncertainty involved. One approach might be to randomly choose between the two options, without considering the rational choice or trying to predict what others will do.

Or, you could take a different perspective and think about what kind of world you want to live in. Do you want to live in a world where people cooperate and work together? If so, then pressing the blue button might be the best choice for you, even if it's not the rational one.

Ultimately, this is a thought-provoking puzzle that highlights the tension between individual self-interest and collective well-being. There is no single "right" answer, and the solution will depend on your personal values and preferences.
